docs.title: Documentation style guide
docs.text: These docs are for customers using GoodBards — marketers, not engineers. Everything below exists to keep 40+ pages sounding like one person wrote them.

docs.title: Who you are writing for
docs.text:
A marketing manager at an agency or mid-market company. They are smart, busy, and not technical. They want to finish a task, not understand the system.

  • Write you, not "the user".
  • Use the words the UI uses. If the button says Launch a Tactic, never call it "initiating a tactic workflow".
  • No internal vocabulary: no tenant, sub-tenant, UID, endpoint, connector config, asset entity. Say your company, account, link.
  • Cut every sentence that does not help them finish the task.

docs.title: Page shape
docs.text:
Every feature page follows the same four headings, in this order:

Heading What goes in it What it's for 2–3 sentences on the problem it solves. Before you start Prerequisites. Delete the section if there are none. How to Numbered steps matching the UI exactly. Good to know Limits, gotchas, and mistakes people actually make.

Readers navigate by pattern. Do not invent new section names.

docs.title: Writing steps
docs.text:
• One action per numbered step.
  • Bold every UI label exactly as it appears: choose Save, not click save.
  • Say where things are: "In the sidebar, choose Audience → Contacts."
  • Stop at the outcome: "Your contacts appear in the list."

docs.title: Screenshots
docs.text:
Screenshots carry more weight than prose for this audience, so they must look consistent. The agreed convention:

Setting Value Tenant Demo tenant only. Never real customer data — this site is public. Theme Light Viewport 1440 × 900 Format PNG, saved to docs/img/screenshots/<page-name>.png

Rules:

  • Never screenshot a real customer's account. Names, email addresses, company names and metrics from a live tenant must not appear. PDPA applies.
  • Screen pages: one screenshot unless a step is genuinely unclear without a second. Guides: one per stage is fine, placed right under the step it shows.
  • Capture the relevant panel, not the whole desktop. Crop out the top bar: it shows the signed-in person's name and photo.
  • Always write real alt text: ![The Contacts list with a segment applied](...). Screen-reader users and broken-image fallbacks both depend on it.
  • Re-capture when the UI changes. A stale screenshot is worse than none.
  • Every screenshot opens full size when clicked (glightbox). To opt one out, add { .no-lightbox } after it.

docs.title: Animated GIFs
docs.text:
Use a GIF only when the movement is the instruction: dragging, an editor interaction, a sequence a still image cannot show (for example inserting a field in the email editor). Everything else stays a PNG.

  • Same rules as screenshots: demo tenant, light theme, the panel only.
  • Short: one action, under 10 seconds, no idle frames at the start or end.
  • Under 2 MB. Save to docs/img/gifs/<page-name>-<action>.gif.
  • Alt text says what happens: ![Choosing Attendee name from Insert field…](...).

docs.title: Admonitions
docs.text:
Use them sparingly — one per page at most.

!!! tip "Save time"
    Duplicate last month's campaign instead of starting over.

!!! warning "This cannot be undone"
    Deleting a segment does not delete its contacts, but the segment is gone.

docs.title: Before you commit
docs.text:
Run the build locally and make sure it is clean:

pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve          # preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict # fails on broken links

--strict is what CI should eventually enforce. Do not add a page to nav: in mkdocs.yml until the file exists, or the build breaks.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: Pushing to main builds and publishes to https://docs.goodbards.ai/ automatically. It takes about a minute. If your change is not live after that, check the Actions tab before assuming DNS.

docs.title: Before you get in touch
docs.text:
Many questions are already answered here:

  • FAQs — the questions we are asked most often.
  • What is GoodBards? — how the platform fits together.
  • Finding Your Way Around — where each feature lives.

If a screen looks different from the documentation, the product may have moved on ahead of these pages — tell us and we will update them.

docs.title: How to reach us
docs.text: Email support@goodbards.com Live chat Bottom right of the app Billing billing@goodbards.com

docs.title: What to include
docs.text:
The more of this you can give us, the faster we can help:

  • What you were trying to do, and what happened instead.
  • The page you were on — the address from your browser is ideal.
  • Your workspace name, shown at the top of the app.
  • A screenshot, if something looks wrong on screen.

Never send us your password

GoodBards support will never ask for your password. If you receive a message claiming to be from us and asking for it, do not reply — forward it to support@goodbards.com.

docs.title: Billing and subscriptions
docs.text:
For invoices, refunds and plan changes, email billing@goodbards.com from the address your account is registered to, and include your workspace name.

To check what your team has used against your plan, see Usage & Billing.

docs.title: How do I reset my password?
docs.text: Go to the login page and choose Forgot Password?. You will receive an email with a reset link.

docs.title: How do I change my name, language or profile picture?
docs.text: In Personal Settings, reached from your profile picture at the top right. See Personal Settings.

docs.title: Can I turn on two-factor authentication?
docs.text: Yes — under Personal Settings → Password & Security. Worth doing: a marketing account can usually email your entire contact database.

docs.title: Why can I not see a section other people mention?
docs.text: What appears in your sidebar depends on your plan and your permissions. Agentic AI in particular is not included in every plan.

docs.title: What should I set up first?
docs.text: Brand & Context, then your Brand Kit, then Connections, then contacts. See Sign Up & Onboarding for why that order.

docs.title: Why is there no data on my analytics pages?
docs.text: Almost always a missing connector. Check Connections — pages such as Google Analytics and Google Trends read from your own accounts and show nothing until those are linked.

docs.title: Some pages take a while to load. Is that normal?
docs.text: Yes. Screens that pull live data from Google can take several seconds. An empty chart usually means it is still loading rather than that there is no data.

docs.title: Does the AI know about my business?
docs.text: It knows what you tell it in Brand & Context — what your company does, how it sounds, who it competes with. Filling that in properly is the single biggest improvement you can make to AI output.

docs.title: Can I control what the AI can see?
docs.text: Yes. Each field in Brand & Context has a Visible to AI / Hide From AI toggle, so you can keep commercially sensitive details out of generated content.

docs.title: Which AI model is used?
docs.text: Set per generation type — text, image, video and audio — in AI Settings. The defaults work well; change them only if you have a specific reason.

docs.title: Does generating content cost anything?
docs.text: It consumes credits from your monthly allowance. Video costs more than images, which cost more than text. Track it in Usage & Billing.

docs.title: What is the difference between a tactic and a campaign?
docs.text: A tactic is one piece of marketing on one channel — a single post, one email. A campaign groups several tactics towards one goal over a period of time. If you just want to publish one post, you want a tactic. See Launch a Tactic.

docs.title: Why is my ad campaign not spending anything?
docs.text: New campaigns start paused, and need at least one enabled ad. See Digital Ads.

docs.title: Can I recall an email after sending it?
docs.text: No. Check your recipient list and send yourself a test first — see Emails.

docs.title: What happens if someone unsubscribes?
docs.text: They move to the unsubscribed group and stop receiving marketing email. Do not work around this by re-importing them — under Singapore's PDPA and equivalent rules elsewhere, opt-outs must be respected.

docs.title: What is the difference between a segment and a mailing list?
docs.text: A segment is a saved rule, re-evaluated each time you use it, so it stays current. A mailing list is a fixed set of contacts. See Contacts.

docs.title: Can I keep separate workspaces for different clients?
docs.text:
Yes, if your plan includes sub-workspaces. Each has its own contacts, campaigns and credit allowance. See Sub-Workspaces.

Not answered here? Contact support.

docs.title: Digital Ads
docs.text:
Plan paid search and follow what your ads bring. In the app, Digital Ads sits under Marketing in the sidebar.

Who sees it: everyone your administrator gives the Digital ads access to.

docs.title: Digital Ads
docs.text:
Your ad campaigns and their results, next to the rest of your marketing.

See Digital Ads.

docs.text:
Research the keywords your market searches for, with volumes and costs, when your Google Ads account is connected.

docs.title: Agentic AI
docs.text:
AI assistants that do marketing work for you — writing, researching, generating images and audio.

Who sees it: everyone your administrator gives the AI studio access to.

docs.title: In this section
docs.text:
• Chat Agents — assistants you hold a conversation with, each set up for a particular kind of work.
  • Workflow Agents — agents that carry out a multi-step task on your behalf.
  • Research Assistant — ask for research on a market, competitor or topic.
  • Image Generation — create images from a description.
  • Video Generation — create short video clips.
  • Text to Speech — turn written copy into spoken audio.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text: Agentic AI is not included in every plan. If this section does not appear in your sidebar, your plan does not include agents.

docs.title: Chat Agents
docs.text: Assistants you can hold a conversation with — each one set up for a particular kind of marketing work.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
A chat agent is an AI assistant you talk to in plain language. Rather than one general-purpose chatbot, GoodBards gives you several, each pointed at a different job: one that understands your brand narrative, one that reads your contact data, one that looks after retention.

Agents know your business. They can draw on your Brand Kit and, depending on the tools they are given, on your campaigns, contacts and analytics.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Chat agents are not available on every plan. If Agentic AI does not appear in your sidebar, your plan does not include agents — speak to your account contact.

docs.title: How to start a chat
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Chat Agents.
  2. Browse the agents, or use Search agents… to find one by name.
  3. Choose the agent that fits what you need, and start typing.

docs.title: Reading an agent card
docs.text:
Each card tells you what the agent is and what it can reach:

On the card What it means Global / Local Global agents are provided by GoodBards. Local agents were created inside your own account. Category The kind of work it is for — General, Data Analysis, Content and Post, Research, Chatbot. Description What the agent is designed to do. Features Capabilities switched on for it. Some agents show No feature enabled yet. Tools What it can actually reach — Marketing Campaigns, Google Analytics, Google Trends and so on.

Tools are the part that matters

Two agents with similar descriptions can behave very differently depending on their tools. An agent with Google Analytics in its tool list can answer questions about your traffic; one without it cannot.

docs.title: Filtering by category
docs.text: The buttons under the title narrow the list: All, Content and Post, Data Analysis, General, Research, Chatbot. A greyed-out category has no agents in it.

docs.title: Creating your own
docs.text: + Create New Agent builds an agent for your account, which appears as Local. Your plan sets how many custom agents you may have.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Agents are not identical. Pick by tools, not by name.
  • An agent only knows what its tools reach. If it cannot see your contacts, it cannot answer questions about them.
  • Global agents are maintained for you. They may gain capabilities over time without you changing anything.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Image Generation
docs.text: Create images for campaigns, posts and emails by describing what you want.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Marketing needs images constantly, and stock photography rarely fits. Describe the image you need and GoodBards creates it — no design software, no photo shoot.

Generated images are useful for social posts, email headers and campaign visuals. They are less suited to anything needing your actual products or people.

docs.title: How to generate an image
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Image Generation.
  2. Describe what you want in Prompt. Detail helps.
  3. Pick an Aspect Ratio.
  4. Open Style Options if you want more control over the look.
  5. Choose Generate Images.

Your images appear under Generated Images on the left.

docs.title: Choosing an aspect ratio
docs.text:
Ratio Shape Good for 1024x1024 Square Instagram posts, profile images. 1536x1024 Landscape Email headers, website banners, LinkedIn. 1024x1536 Portrait Stories, vertical mobile formats. auto Chosen for you When you are not sure.

Pick the ratio for where the image will be used. Cropping a square image into a banner afterwards usually spoils the composition.

docs.title: Writing a good prompt
docs.text:
Be specific about subject, setting, style and mood. "A flat-lay of tropical fruit on a pale marble table, bright daylight, minimal styling" gives a far better result than "fruit picture".

AI Assist writes the prompt for you

AI Assist, above the prompt box, expands a rough idea into a fuller description. Useful when you know what you want but not how to describe it.

docs.title: Choosing a model
docs.text: Model at the top sets which AI generates the image. The default comes from your company's AI Settings; change it here to use a different one for this image.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Generation uses credits. Each image counts against your allowance — see Usage & Billing.
  • Expect to iterate. The first result is rarely the one you use. Adjust the prompt and generate again.
  • Check faces, hands and text. AI images still get these wrong, and mistakes are more obvious to your audience than to you.
  • Do not generate real people or brands. Images resembling identifiable people or another company's branding carry legal risk.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Research Assistant
docs.text: Ask a question about a market, competitor or topic, and get a researched answer back.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Some questions need more than a quick answer — what are the main loyalty programmes among Singapore F&B chains, and how do they differ? The Research Assistant works through questions like that properly rather than replying off the top of its head.

Use it for market scans, competitor comparisons and background before a campaign. For quick drafting, a chat agent is faster.

docs.title: How to request research
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Research Assistant.
  2. Type your question in the box at the bottom.
  3. Send it, and wait — this takes longer than an ordinary chat reply.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The assistant takes four steps, which is why it is slower and better than a single answer:

Stage What happens Ask Your Question You describe what you want to know. Be specific. Break It Down Your question is split into smaller subtopics to explore from several angles. Research in Depth Each subtopic is examined and the findings pulled together. Get Your Results You get a fuller, more rounded answer than a quick reply would give.

Specific questions get better research

"Tell me about coffee" produces something bland. "How do specialty coffee brands in Singapore position themselves against chains, and what do they charge?" gives the assistant something to work with.

docs.title: Chat History
docs.text: Chat History, at the top right, holds your previous research. Worth checking before asking again — someone may already have researched the same ground.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Responses take a while. The screen says so, and that is the trade-off for depth. Ask, then come back to it.
  • Research costs credits. More than a simple chat, because it runs several searches. See Usage & Billing.
  • Verify anything load-bearing. Check facts you plan to publish — prices, statistics and competitor claims especially.
  • It is a starting point. Use the research to inform your own judgement, not to replace it.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Text to Speech
docs.text: Turn written copy into spoken audio, in a voice you choose.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Some audiences listen rather than read. Text to Speech produces audio from your written copy — useful for video voiceovers, social clips, accessible versions of written content, and audio ads.

You write the script; the platform reads it aloud.

docs.title: How to generate audio
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Text to Speech.
  2. Paste or type your script into Text. The limit is 5,000 characters.
  3. Pick a Voice.
  4. Choose Generate Audio.

Your audio appears under Audio Preview on the left.

docs.title: Choosing a voice
docs.text:
Each voice has a short description of how it sounds:

Voice Character Kore Warm, female Charon Deep, male Puck Energetic, neutral Fenrir Strong, male Aoede Soft, female Leda Clear, female

Match the voice to the content. Energetic suits a product launch; warm or soft suits something more considered.

Pick one voice and stay with it

If audio becomes a regular part of your marketing, using the same voice each time makes it recognisable. Switching voices between clips sounds like different companies talking.

docs.title: Writing for the ear
docs.text:
Copy that reads well on a page often sounds wrong aloud. Shorter sentences work better, and it is worth reading your script out before generating it.

AI Assist, above the text box, can help adapt written copy into something that sounds natural spoken.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• 5,000 characters is roughly five minutes. Longer scripts need splitting.
  • Listen before you publish. Check names, acronyms and any local place names — these are where pronunciation goes wrong.
  • Generation uses credits. See Usage & Billing.
  • Say if audio is synthetic where your audience would reasonably expect a real person.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Video Generation
docs.text: Create short video clips from a written description.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Short video performs well on social, and producing it normally means a camera, an editor and a week. This generates a clip from a description instead — useful for social posts, ad creative and background footage.

Clips are short by design: a few seconds, suited to social rather than long-form storytelling.

docs.title: How to generate a video
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Video Generation.
  2. Describe the clip you want in Prompt.
  3. Pick an Aspect Ratio and a Duration.
  4. Choose Generate Video.

Your clip appears under Video Preview on the left.

docs.title: Aspect ratio
docs.text:
Ratio Use it for 16:9 Landscape YouTube, website embeds, presentations. 9:16 Portrait Stories, Reels, TikTok — anything watched on a phone held upright.

Choose before generating. Cropping landscape footage into portrait afterwards cuts the sides off your subject.

docs.title: Duration
docs.text: Clips run from 5s to 8s. Shorter is usually better on social, where the first two seconds decide whether anyone keeps watching.

docs.title: Writing a good prompt
docs.text:
Describe the shot the way you would brief a videographer — subject, movement, setting, light. The placeholder on screen is a good model: a cinematic drone shot flying over misty mountains at sunrise.

AI Assist above the prompt box expands a rough idea into a fuller description.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Video costs more than images. Generation is slower and uses more credits — see Usage & Billing.
  • Expect several attempts. Getting the motion right usually takes a few tries, so allow time before a deadline.
  • Watch for artefacts. Faces, hands and text are where AI video still fails. Watch the clip fully before publishing.
  • Add captions. Most social video is watched with the sound off.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Workflow Agents
docs.text: Multi-step jobs that run themselves — research, analysis and planning that would take you an afternoon.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
A chat agent answers a question. A workflow agent carries out a whole process: researching a company, comparing it with competitors, ranking them, and producing a SWOT analysis — each step feeding the next.

You start it and come back to the result.

docs.title: How to run a workflow
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Workflow Agents.
  2. Browse the workflows, or filter by category.
  3. Read the diagram to see what it will do.
  4. Choose Start Workflow.

docs.title: Reading the diagram
docs.text:
Each workflow shows its steps as a flow chart, so you can see what happens before you start it. A company research workflow, for example, runs:

Start → Company Research → Competition Analysis → Competition Ranking → SWOT Analysis

Some workflows fan out and rejoin — splitting a question into parts, working on each separately, then merging the findings. That is why they take longer than a single answer and produce a more thorough one.

Read the diagram first

The flow chart tells you what the agent will actually do. If the steps do not match what you need, a different workflow — or a chat agent — may suit you better.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
Filter with the buttons under the title: All, Campaign and Execution, Operational, Strategy and Planning, Tactics. A greyed-out category has no workflows in it.

Use Search agents… to find one by name.

docs.title: Chat History
docs.text: Chat History on each workflow holds previous runs. Worth checking before starting a fresh one — a colleague may have run the same analysis last month.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Results are not instant. These run several steps in sequence; expect to come back to them.
  • Workflows use more credits than a chat. Each step costs. See Usage & Billing.
  • Check the output before acting on it. A workflow producing competitor analysis is a starting point for your judgement, not a decision.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Audience
docs.text:
Everyone you market to: the people, the organisations they work for, and how they engage with you.

Who sees it: everyone your administrator gives the Audience access to. Depending on their role, a colleague may see only the contacts they own.

docs.title: Contacts
docs.text:
The people you market to, with their details, custom fields, status and history of every email, form and event. Group them into segments that update themselves as contacts change.

See Contacts.

docs.title: Companies
docs.text:
The organisations your contacts belong to, with their own segments.

See Companies.

docs.title: Mailing lists
docs.text:
Lists people subscribe to, for example from a sign-up form. A contact who unsubscribes stays unsubscribed: adding them again by hand does not override their choice.

See Mailing lists.

docs.title: Adding contacts
docs.text:
Add one contact, import a spreadsheet with Bulk Add Contacts, or photograph a business card with Scan Business Card. Import Jobs shows how each import went.

Guide coming soon

docs.title: Lead scoring
docs.text:
A 0–100 score per contact, from what they did: opened, clicked, registered, attended. Use it to see who is ready for a sales conversation.

Guide coming soon

docs.title: Why this comes first
docs.text: Almost everything else depends on your audience. Emails need recipients, forms create contacts, and reporting is only as good as the data behind it. If you are setting up GoodBards for the first time, get contacts in before building campaigns.

docs.title: Companies
docs.text: The organisations your contacts work for — and how complete your picture of them is.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
In B2B marketing the company matters as much as the person. Several contacts may work at the same organisation, and a decision usually involves more than one of them.

Companies group your contacts by the organisation they belong to, so you can see account-level activity rather than isolated individuals.

docs.title: Reading the Companies home
docs.text:
Audience → Companies opens on Home, which summarises your data rather than listing organisations.

Tile What it tells you Total Companies How many organisations you hold. No Main Contact Companies with nobody nominated as the primary contact. Linked Contacts Contacts successfully attached to a company.

No Main Contact is the number to fix

A company with no main contact means you have the organisation but no named person to approach. If this figure is close to your total, your account data is not yet usable for outreach.

docs.title: Company Readiness
docs.text:
The charts below score how complete your data is:

  • Company Database Count — how it has grown.
  • Database Growth — the rate of growth.
  • Field Completeness — the percentage of fields filled in. Low completeness limits how well you can segment.
  • Distribution by Industry — which sectors you hold. Companies with no industry set show as Unknown.
  • Distribution by Company Size — the spread from small to large.

The letter badge beside Company Readiness grades your data overall. Treat a low grade as a prompt to fill in missing fields rather than a problem with the platform.

docs.title: Adding companies
docs.text: Add them directly, or let them arrive with your contacts — importing contacts that include a company name creates the organisations for you.

docs.title: Other tabs
docs.text: Tab What it holds Details List Individual company records. Segments Saved filters over companies. Custom Fields Extra fields you add. Custom Lists Your own groupings.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Unknown industry limits targeting. You cannot segment by a field you have not filled in.
  • Link contacts to companies. An unlinked contact cannot be counted towards the account they work for.
  • Nominate a main contact. It is who the platform treats as your route into that organisation.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Contacts
docs.text: The people you market to — how to add them, keep their details current, and group them into segments.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Every email you send and every form someone fills in comes back to a contact. Contacts are the centre of the platform: get them right and the rest of your marketing has something to work with.

docs.title: Adding contacts
docs.text:
There is more than one way, depending on how many you have:

Method Use it when Add one at a time You met someone and want them in straight away. Import You have a list to bring across. Progress shows under Import Jobs. Card Scanner You came back from an event with a stack of business cards. Scan them and the details are read for you. Forms Someone signs up themselves. See Forms.

docs.title: Reading the Contacts home
docs.text:
Audience → Contacts opens on the Home tab, which summarises your database rather than listing individuals.

The tiles across the top tell you:

  • Total Contacts — how many you hold, and how many your plan allows. The bar fills as you approach the limit.
  • Subscribed — contacts who have agreed to hear from you.
  • Regular — contacts with no marketing consent yet: you can work with them, but not email them marketing.
  • Others (unsubscribed, do not contact) — people you must not email.

Subscribed is the number that matters

A large database is not much use if most of it has unsubscribed. Only Subscribed contacts can receive marketing email.

Score Progression below tracks engagement over time, and Contact Readiness shows how complete and usable your data is.

docs.title: Finding individual contacts
docs.text:
The Details List tab lists every contact: their code, name, owner, email, status and last update.

  • Search by name or email, and choose the columns to show with View.
  • Each contact can have owners, the colleagues responsible for them. Filter by owner, or select contacts and choose Assign Owners. Depending on their role, a colleague may only see the contacts they own.
  • Export As CSV downloads the list; Add Contact creates one.
  • Click a contact's code to open their record: details, custom fields, mailing lists, and the history of every email, form and event.

docs.title: Segments
docs.text:
A segment is a saved filter — a rule that decides who belongs, evaluated when you use it, so it stays current as contacts change.

To create one, open the Segments tab and choose Add Segment, then set the rule — location, job title, behaviour, or any custom field you have added.

Useful segments look like:

  • Singapore members — everyone in one market
  • Corporate buyers — one type of customer
  • Bangkok launch list — the people from one event

Segments beat one-off filters

If you find yourself applying the same filter repeatedly, save it as a segment. Give it a description too — in six months you will not remember what the rule was.

docs.title: Other tabs
docs.text: Tab What it holds Mailing Lists Lists people subscribe to. See Mailing lists. Custom Fields Extra fields you add to hold what matters to your business. Custom Lists Your own groupings. Import Jobs The status of imports, including any rows that failed.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Segments update themselves; mailing lists do not. A segment re-evaluates its rule each time; a mailing list stays as you built it.
  • Watch your plan limit. The Total Contacts bar shows how close you are.
  • Respect unsubscribes. Under Singapore's PDPA and equivalent rules elsewhere, contacts who opt out must not receive marketing email. GoodBards excludes them, but do not work around it by re-importing them.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Mailing lists
docs.text: Lists people subscribe to, such as your newsletter or a members' club, with their consent kept for each list.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: A segment is a rule; a mailing list is a commitment. When someone joins a list, from a sign-up form or because you added them, they agreed to receive what that list sends. GoodBards keeps each person's status per list, so you always know who may receive what, and an unsubscribe is respected everywhere.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • Contacts to add, or a form people can sign up with.

docs.title: How to manage a mailing list
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Audience → Contacts, then the Mailing Lists tab. Each list shows its description and number of members.

  2. To create one, choose New Mailing List, then give it a name and a description.

  3. Click a list to open it. The counters show who is Subscribed, Pending, Unsubscribed, and Not on list.

  4. Below, each member shows their contact status, their status on this list, and how they joined. Revoke takes someone off the list.

  5. Embed Form gives you a sign-up form for your own website that adds people to this list.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Unsubscribed means locked. Someone who unsubscribed from a list cannot be added back, or removed, by anyone on your team. Only they can re-subscribe. This is how GoodBards keeps you compliant with PDPA and similar laws.

  • Email the list from a campaign. When you send an email, choose the list as the audience. See Emails.

GoodBards is an Agentic AI Marketing OS — a single platform where AI agents plan, create and execute marketing campaigns, while remembering your brand's voice, data and history.

In practice that means the work you would normally spread across an email tool, a social scheduler, a CRM and a folder of brand assets happens in one place, with AI that already knows your business.

This documentation is a user guide: how to do things, screen by screen. For what GoodBards offers and why, see goodbards.com.

docs.title: Run an event from start to finish
docs.text: From the first invitation to the thank-you email: everything an in-person, online or hybrid event needs, in the order you will do it. Allow about an hour to set up your first event; later ones go faster because you can duplicate them.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: An event touches every part of your marketing: your audience, a landing page, a registration form, several emails, check-in at the door and the follow-up. GoodBards keeps all of it on one event page, and every guest who registers becomes a contact you can market to afterwards.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your Brand Kit, so the landing page and emails look like you. See Brand Kit.
  • The people you will invite, as a segment or a mailing list. See Contacts.

docs.title: 1. Create the event
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Marketing → Event Management. Your events are listed as cards, with their status, date, place and registrations.

  2. Choose New Event, then give it a name, a date and time, and a place.

  3. Open the event. It starts on the Overview: registrations against capacity, invitations sent, days to go, and quick actions such as Copy Registration Link. The tabs follow the life of the event, from left to right.

The dots on a tab show it is set up. Everything saves on its own: there is no Save button on the event page.

docs.title: 2. Describe the event
docs.text:
On the Definition tab:

  1. Set the Event Type, the Format (in person, online or hybrid) and the Visibility.

  2. Under About the event, write a Short Description, the Address, and choose a Cover Image. These appear on the landing page and in every email.

  3. For an online or hybrid event, add the Join link. Only confirmed guests receive it.

The event's name, date and place in every email come from this tab. To change them, change them here, never inside an email.

The Landing page tab shows the page guests register on, built from what you just wrote. To change its layout, choose Duplicate to customize.

docs.title: 3. Prepare the registration
docs.text:
On the Registration tab:

  1. Under Settings, set the Max Capacity, when registration opens and closes, and whether to Require Approval.

  2. Turn on the Waitlist if the event can fill up, and choose how a freed seat is given: Automatic (the next person in line is seated and emailed) or Manual (you choose).

  3. The blocks below are folded; click a title to open one.

  4. Under Registration form, keep the default form (name, email, company, job title) or choose one of your own. See Forms.

  5. Under Contact registration, check which form fields fill in the contact: email, first and last name, and anything else you want to keep with Add Mapping. Changes save on their own.

docs.title: 4. Set up the emails
docs.text:
Each guest receives the right email for their situation automatically. Under Registration emails, the list shows the emails your event can send, and grows when you turn on approval or the waitlist.

To change one:

  1. Open it and choose Edit on the preview.
  2. Change the Subject at the top and the text in the editor, then choose Apply.

The invitation and the reminders work the same way, on the Communications tab. See Editing an email.

docs.title: 5. Invite your audience
docs.text:
1. On the Communications tab, under Invitation email, choose the audience to invite.
  2. Choose Send Invitations. You can also send them from the Actions menu.
  3. Add Registration reminders for people who have not registered yet, and Event reminders for guests, for example one day and one hour before.

At the bottom of the tab, Sent emails lists every email the event has sent, with the number of recipients.

To announce the event on social media, see Social Post.

docs.title: 6. Manage registrations
docs.text:
The Attendance tab lists every guest, their status and the last email they received.

  • Approve or decline requests when approval is on.
  • ↑ Promote a waiting guest when the waitlist is in Manual mode.
  • Add Attendee to register someone yourself, for example from a phone call.
  • The eye icon opens a guest's history with this event: what was sent, delivered, opened and clicked. Useful when a guest says they never got their confirmation.

docs.title: 7. On the day
docs.text:
Every confirmed guest has a QR code in their confirmation and reminder emails.

  1. Open the Actions menu.
  2. Choose Scan attendee to check guests in with your phone or laptop camera, or Kiosk mode to let them check themselves in at the entrance.

  3. To print name badges, set the format under Attendance → Badge, then use the print icon on a guest's row.

docs.title: 8. Follow up
docs.text:
1. When the event is over, choose Actions → End event. Guests who were not checked in are marked as absent.
  2. On the Follow-up tab, set the email for those who attended, those who did not, and those you invited who never registered. Attach a survey form if you want feedback.

  3. On the Analytics tab, see registrations broken down by status or by any form field, and choose Email Performance to see how every event email did.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Publish before you share the link. A draft event does not accept registrations.
  • Cancel a registration with ⊘, not with the status menu. ⊘ emails the guest and offers the seat to the waitlist; the status menu only corrects the list.
  • Every guest becomes a contact. After the event, find them in your audience and follow up with a normal email or campaign.
  • Next time, duplicate. Duplicating an event copies its settings, emails and form, so only the date and details change.
