docs.title: Where to start
docs.text: Read Launch a Tactic first. It explains the difference between a tactic and a campaign, which the rest of this section builds on.

docs.title: Campaigns
docs.text: Group related marketing activity under one plan, with a shared objective and a start and end date.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
A campaign is a container for everything you are doing towards one goal — a product launch, an event, a seasonal push. Instead of tracking a dozen separate posts and emails, you see them together and track whether the goal is being met.

If you only want to publish one post or one email, you do not need a campaign. Use Launch a Tactic instead.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Know your objective — for example Product Launch, Brand Awareness, or Networking With Industry Professionals. You choose one when you create the campaign.
  • Know roughly when the campaign should start and finish.

docs.title: How to create a campaign
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Marketing → Campaigns.
  2. Choose + Create New Campaign.
  3. Give it a name, pick an objective, and set the start and end dates.
  4. Add the tactics that belong to it — the posts, emails and events that work towards the objective.

docs.title: Reading the campaign list
docs.text:
The four tiles across the top summarise where things stand: Total, Active, Pending and Completed Campaigns.

Each row in the table shows the campaign's objective, its status, and the dates it runs between. Sort by any column using the arrows beside the heading.

Status What it means Pending Created, but not started yet. Active Currently running. Ended Finished.

docs.title: Inside a campaign
docs.text:
Click a campaign's name to open it. Its tabs are Overview, Budget, Calendar and Analytics.

Overview shows the Campaign Details: objective, budget, target industry, audience, regions, and a description the AI uses as context whenever it writes for this campaign. Choose the pencil to change them.

Below, Tactics lists everything the campaign runs: ads, blog posts, social posts, emails and events, each with its status and end date.

  • Add Tactic adds one yourself.
  • Plan With AI suggests the tactics that fit the campaign's objective.
  • Write Content With AI drafts the content of the tactics.

docs.title: The campaign report
docs.text: The Analytics tab gathers the results of every tactic in one place: reach and engagement on social networks, email deliveries, opens and clicks, event registrations and attendance, and ad spend and returns. Each figure shows its change against the previous report. Use the arrows to move between report dates, or History to see them all.

docs.title: Starting and stopping
docs.text:
The Start / Stop column controls whether a campaign is running:

  • ▶ Start begins a pending campaign.
  • ⏸ Pause stops an active one.

Pausing does not delete anything — it stops further activity until you start it again.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• A campaign is a plan, not a channel. Publishing still happens through the individual tactics inside it.
  • Name campaigns so you can find them later. Something like Q4-2026-Product-Launch is easier to search than New campaign.
  • End dates are not deadlines. A campaign past its end date stays visible in the list; the date describes the plan, it does not stop work by itself.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Digital Ads
docs.text: Manage your paid advertising — campaigns, keywords, conversion tracking and reporting — without leaving GoodBards.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Paid advertising is where marketing budget turns into traffic, and where it disappears fastest if nobody is watching. This brings your ad campaigns and their performance in beside the rest of your marketing, so spend can be judged against everything else you are doing.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Your Google Ads account must be connected. See Connections.

Google Ads today; Meta and LinkedIn to follow

Google Ads is available now. Meta Ads and LinkedIn Ads appear marked Soon and cannot be used yet.

docs.title: Getting your first campaign live
docs.text:
New campaigns do not start spending on their own. The three steps are:

  1. Create a campaign — on the Campaigns tab, launch a Search campaign with its daily budget. New campaigns start paused.
  2. Add ad groups & keywords — structure the campaign and choose the searches you want to appear for.
  3. Enable it to go live — a campaign needs at least one enabled ad. Enabling it is the moment spend starts.

Nothing spends until you enable it

A campaign sitting at zero spend is usually paused rather than broken. That is deliberate — it stops half-built campaigns burning budget. Check the campaign is enabled and has at least one enabled ad.

docs.title: Reading the overview
docs.text:
Set the period with the date selector, then read the four headline figures:

Metric What it means Total spend What you have spent, in your account currency. Conversions How many people did the thing you were paying for. Blended ROAS Return on ad spend — revenue divided by spend. 2.00x means two dollars back for every one spent. CTR Click-through rate: the share of people who clicked after seeing your ad.

ROAS is the number that decides whether a campaign continues. CTR tells you whether the ad itself is working — a low CTR usually means the ad copy or the keywords are wrong, not the budget.

Below, Spend by channel shows daily spend stacked by channel, and Budget allocation shows how spend is split across campaigns.

docs.title: The tabs
docs.text: Tab What it covers Overview The summary above. Campaigns Create and manage campaigns, ad groups and keywords. Recommendations Suggested improvements to your account. Conversion Tracking Defining what counts as a conversion. Callouts Extra text shown alongside your ads. Settings Account-level configuration.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Conversion tracking first. Without it, ROAS and conversions stay at zero and you are flying blind. Set it up before spending.
  • Start with a small daily budget. Raise it once you can see which keywords convert. It is much easier to increase spend than to recover it.
  • Check your currency. Spend is shown in the account currency — SGD in the example above.
  • Judge over weeks, not days. Early figures are noisy; give a campaign enough clicks to mean something before rewriting it.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Emails
docs.text: Design, send and track the emails you send to your contacts — from a one-off announcement to a regular newsletter.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Email is where most marketing plans still start. GoodBards keeps the whole job in one place: you pick a look, write the message, choose who receives it, and see how it performed — without exporting lists or switching to a separate email tool.

Because your emails sit alongside your contacts, anything you already know about your audience is available when you choose recipients.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• At least one contact in Audience → Contacts, or a mailing list to send to.
  • Your Brand Kit set up, if you want emails to pick up your colours and logo automatically. See Brand Kit.

docs.title: How to create an email
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Marketing → Emails.
  2. Choose + Create Email.
  3. Pick how you want to start. GoodBards offers four options:
Option When to use it Designs Gallery The usual choice. Reuse a look and feel — header, footer and branding — and just write the message. Marked Recommended. Import from External You already have the email elsewhere. Paste HTML, upload a .eml file, or fetch a URL. Reuse existing from platform Send something you have written before, with fresh recipients. Start Blank An empty email with no styling. Best for a plain, personal message.
  1. Work through the three steps at the top of the dialog: Look & Feel, then Content, then Recipients.
  2. Preview your email before sending, and send yourself a test if you can.

Reuse beats starting over

If you send a similar email regularly, Reuse existing from platform keeps the content and design and only asks for new recipients — usually faster than building it again.

docs.title: Finding your emails
docs.text:
Everything you have created is listed under Email Gallery, on the Emails tab. Use the search box to find one by name, and the buttons beside it to switch between grid and list view.

The Email Designs tab holds the reusable looks — headers, footers and branding — rather than individual messages.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Emails and designs are separate. A design is the wrapper you reuse; an email is one message you send. Editing a design does not rewrite emails already sent.
  • Check the preview before every send. Email clients vary, and a layout that looks right in the editor can shift in Gmail or Outlook.
  • Sent emails cannot be recalled. Confirm your recipient list before the final step.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Event Management
docs.text: Run an event end to end: the registration page, the emails your guests receive, the waitlist, check-in on the day, and the follow-up afterwards.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Events usually mean juggling a registration page, a spreadsheet of attendees, a handful of emails and a clipboard at the door. Event Management keeps all of it on one page, and because every registration becomes a contact, following up afterwards does not mean re-typing a list.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An email design for your brand, if you want the event emails to look like your other emails. Without one, they use the standard GoodBards design.
  • A form, if the default registration form (name, email, company, job title) is not enough.

docs.title: How to set up an event
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Marketing → Event Management.
  2. Choose New Event and fill in the name, type, date, time and venue.
  3. Open the event. Its tabs follow the life of the event, left to right: Overview, Definition, Landing page, Registration, Communications, Attendance, Analytics, Follow-up.
  4. Work through them in that order. Everything saves on its own; there is no Save button on the event page.

docs.title: Definition: what guests see
docs.text: The Definition tab holds the cover image, the short and long descriptions, the date and the address. These feed the landing page and every event email: the event name, date and place in your emails always come from here. Change them here, never inside an email.

docs.title: Landing page
docs.text:
The Landing page tab shows the page guests register on. It is built from the Definition tab, so it is always up to date.

To change its layout, choose Duplicate to customize. You get your own copy in the visual editor.

A customized page is a copy

Once you customize the landing page, later changes on the Definition tab are no longer copied into it. Update the page yourself, or go back to the default.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
• Settings: capacity, the registration window, Require Approval, and the Waitlist.
  • Registration form: keep the default form, or choose Create new or Duplicate existing to use one of your own. Edit form opens it.
  • Contact registration: which form fields fill the contact record (email, first and last name, phone, job title, tags, custom fields). See Forms.
  • Registration emails: one email for each situation a guest can be in (see below).
  • Confirmation message: the text shown on the page after registering.

The last four blocks are folded; click a title to open it.

docs.title: Registration emails
docs.text:
Each email is sent automatically when a guest reaches that situation. Only the ones your event can produce are listed:

Email Sent when Listed when Confirmed The guest has a seat. Carries the check-in QR code and calendar links. Always Request received The guest registered and waits for your approval. Require Approval is on Approved You approved the request. Require Approval is on Declined You declined the request. You can turn this one off. Require Approval is on On the waitlist The event was full; the guest joined the waitlist. Waitlist is on Spot opened A seat freed up and the guest moved off the waitlist. Waitlist is on

docs.title: Editing an email
docs.text:
Every event email (the registration emails above, and the invitation and reminders under Communications) works the same way. The card shows the email as guests receive it, inside your event design.

  1. Click the preview, or Edit. The editor opens, with the Subject at the top and Visual, Code and AI on the side.
  2. Change the text, then choose Apply. The card now says Your own version of this email.
  3. To go back, choose Reset to standard.

In the Visual editor:

  • Purple dashed boxes are parts only some guests see. The title says who, for example Shown when the guest has a check-in QR code. Edit the text inside; the box itself cannot be moved or deleted, so the email keeps working for every guest.
  • Purple chips, such as Attendee name or Event location, are filled in for each guest when the email is sent. To add one, click into a text and pick it from Insert field… in the text toolbar. Do not type them by hand.

To send an email you built under Emails instead, choose Use one of my emails instead under the card.

docs.title: How to send, and see what happened
docs.text:
1. On Communications, choose Send Invitations to email your audience, or Send Reminder Now for a reminder.

  2. At the bottom of the tab, Sent emails lists every email the event has sent, with the time, the number of recipients and who sent it. Confirmations and other one-by-one emails are grouped per day.

  3. Choose Recipients on a line to see who received it, search them, or show the failed ones only. Choose Metrics for opens and clicks.

  4. On Attendance, the Latest email column shows the last email each guest received. The eye icon opens the guest's History with this event: what was sent, delivered, opened and clicked.

  5. On Analytics, Email Performance shows all the event's emails together or one type at a time, and Export CSV downloads the list.

docs.title: The waitlist
docs.text:
Turn on Waitlist under Registration › Settings. When the event is full, new registrations join a queue. Choose how a freed seat is given:

  • Automatic: the next person in line gets it and is emailed.
  • Manual: you choose. On Attendance, use ↑ Promote on a waiting guest. It only works when a seat is free.

docs.title: Checking people in
docs.text: On the day, use Scan attendee to check people in. Each guest's confirmation and reminder emails carry a QR code; scanning it records them as attended.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Publish before you share the link. A draft event does not accept registrations.
  • Declined guests can stay unaware. Turn off the Declined email and nobody you decline is emailed, even when you change a status by hand.
  • Cancel with ⊘, not with the status menu. Cancel registration (the ⊘ icon on a row) emails the guest and offers the seat to the waitlist. Changing the status from the menu only corrects the list.
  • Follow up while it is fresh. Attendees are contacts, so the Follow-up tab can email everyone who came, everyone who did not, or the people you invited who never registered.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Forms
docs.text: Collect sign-ups, registrations and feedback, and have the responses flow into your audience automatically.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
A form is how people tell you something: registering for an event, asking to be contacted, or rating an experience. Responses land in GoodBards rather than in a spreadsheet, so the people who reply become contacts you can market to.

Forms are also how you run satisfaction surveys (NPS, CSAT and similar) without a separate survey tool.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • A privacy statement, if you collect personal data: Brand & Context → General Information → Privacy Statements. Mark one as the company default and every form uses it unless you pick another.

docs.title: How to create a form
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Marketing → Forms, then Create Form.

  2. Choose how to start:

    • Form Gallery (recommended): ready-made forms grouped by what they measure, such as Contact / demo request, Net Promoter Score (NPS), Event registration or Newsletter signup.
    • Reuse a form: a copy of one of your own forms.
    • Import: paste the HTML of a form you already have.
    • Start blank: an empty contact form.
    • Fill in Core definition: the Name, a Category and a Description.
    • Choose Edit form to change the fields (see below).
    • Choose Create. Set the form to Open when it should accept responses.

docs.title: Change the fields
docs.text:
Edit form opens the visual builder.

  • Add a field: drag it from Forms in the left panel: Text field, Email field, Phone field, Multi-line text, Dropdown, Checkbox, Consent.
  • Reorder: drag a field to its new place.
  • Make a field required: select it, open its settings (the gear icon on the right) and tick Required.
  • Choose Apply to keep your changes.

docs.title: Turn responses into contacts
docs.text:
In the Customer Data Platform block:

  1. Switch on Create CRM contact.
  2. Check the mapping table. Email must point to the field that holds the person's email address. First name and Last name are recommended.
  3. To fill more of the contact, choose Add Mapping and pick a contact field (Phone, Job title, Tags or one of your custom fields). Fill it from a Form field, or with a Fixed value (for example, tag everyone who replies with webinar-oct).
  4. Under Privacy statement, keep Company default or pick another statement.

docs.title: Use a form to register for an event
docs.text: Open the event, then Registration → Registration form. Pick your form, or choose Create new to start from the event registration template. The event then manages the form's confirmation email and thank-you page, under Registration → Confirmation. See Event Management.

docs.title: Categories and status
docs.text:
Category Use it for Registration & sign-ups Event registration, newsletter and webinar sign-ups. Experience metrics Satisfaction surveys: NPS, CSAT, CES, star ratings. Feedback & research Event and product feedback, general surveys. Data capture Contact and demo requests.

A form is a Draft while you build it and Open when it accepts responses. The list shows Submissions and Views for each form: many views and few submissions usually means the form asks too much.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Consent is only recorded when the box is ticked. A form records a person's acceptance of your privacy statement only if it has a Consent field and they tick it. Without one, the editor warns you: drag the Consent block in.
  • A form must be Open to collect anything, even if you have shared the link.
  • Responses update existing contacts. A submission with an email address you already hold fills in that contact's empty fields; it never overwrites what is there.
  • Renaming a field is safe. The contact mapping follows the new name.
  • One form, one event. Picking a form already used by another event links a copy, so the two events never share answers.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Launch a Tactic
docs.text: Put out a single piece of marketing — one post, one email — without setting up a whole campaign first.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
A tactic is one piece of marketing activity on one channel: a LinkedIn post, a TikTok video, an email newsletter. It is the smallest thing you can publish.

Most of the time you do not need a campaign. If you simply want something out on Instagram this afternoon, start here. Campaigns are for when several tactics work towards the same goal over a period of time — see Campaigns.

docs.title: How to launch a tactic
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Marketing → Launch a Tactic.
  2. Pick the channel you want to publish on.

Channels are grouped by type, and each says what it is best suited to — LinkedIn for professional and B2B content, TikTok for short-form video, and so on. Once you have picked one, follow the steps for that channel to write your content and publish or schedule it.

Not sure which channel?

The short description under each one is a reminder of what that audience expects. Match the content to the channel rather than posting the same message everywhere.

docs.title: Available channels
docs.text:
Group Channels Social Media Twitter, Reddit, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Short YouTube Video, YouTube Video, Telegram, WhatsApp Emails Email Campaign — targeted newsletters and promotional emails

Use Search tactics… at the top right to jump straight to one.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• You need the channel connected first. A social channel you have not linked cannot publish. Set these up in Settings → Connections.
  • A tactic can be added to a campaign later. Starting with a single tactic does not lock you out of organising it into a campaign afterwards.
  • Each channel has its own rules on length, images and video. The tactic screen for that channel will tell you what it accepts.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Configure your account, your company, your brand and the services GoodBards connects to.

Who sees it: your own Personal Settings are open to everyone. Everything else needs the Settings access.

docs.title: Personal Settings
docs.text:
Your profile, password, language, default brand voice and your own AI memory.

See Personal Settings.

docs.title: Brand & Context
docs.text:
What the AI knows about your company: general information, privacy statements, your marketing campaign defaults, competitors and website.

See Brand & Context and How the AI knows your brand.

docs.title: Brand Kit
docs.text:
Logos, colours, fonts and tone of voice, used by every email, design and AI answer.

See Brand Kit.

docs.title: Voices Bank
docs.text:
Writing styles learned from real samples, such as your founder's posts.

See How the AI knows your brand.

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text:
Link the outside services you use: social networks, Google Analytics and Search Console, Google Ads, your CRM.

See Connections.

docs.title: AI Settings
docs.text:
Which AI models your team uses, the tools and skills agents may use, and what the agents have learned.

See AI Settings.

docs.title: Users, roles & permissions
docs.text:
Invite colleagues and decide what each one can see and change. Access is given per module (Home, Audience, Marketing, Emails and forms, Events, Social media, Digital ads, Content hub, Website and SEO, AI studio, Tool box, Settings), each in read-only or read and write. Ready-made roles cover the usual cases: a Marketer sees everything, a Sales member sees the Audience and only the contacts they own.

See Users, roles & permissions.

docs.title: Sub-workspaces
docs.text:
Separate workspaces under your own, one per client, brand or business unit.

See Sub-Workspaces.

docs.title: Usage & Billing
docs.text:
What your team has used against your plan.

See Usage & Billing.

docs.title: Setting up for the first time
docs.text: In this order: Brand & Context, then Brand Kit, then Connections. The brand kit shapes everything the AI produces, so it is worth doing before generating content.

docs.title: AI Settings
docs.text: Choose which AI models your team uses, and what the AI is allowed to do.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
GoodBards can use different AI providers and models for different jobs. Most teams never need to change this — the defaults are sensible. It matters when you have a preference about which provider handles your content, or want a higher-quality model for one kind of work.

Changing a model here affects everyone in your company.

docs.title: How to change a default model
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Settings → AI Settings.
  2. On the Models tab, find the type of generation you want to change.
  3. Pick a Provider, then a Large Language Model (LLM) from that provider.

docs.title: The four generation types
docs.text:
Type Used for Text generation Writing — email copy, social posts, agent replies. Image generation Images created from a description. Video Generation Short video clips. Audio Generation Text to speech.

Each is set independently, so you can use one provider for writing and another for images.

Not every type needs to be set

A generation type showing Select Provider has no model configured. Those features will not work until you choose one.

docs.title: The other tabs
docs.text: Tab What it holds Models Default model per generation type, as above. MCP Tools External tools your agents may use. Skills Capabilities available to your agents. Learned Memory What the AI has remembered about your business over time.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• These are company-wide defaults. Changing a model changes it for every colleague, not just you.
  • Models differ in cost as well as quality. A more capable model consumes credits faster — see Usage & Billing.
  • Test after changing. Generate a sample piece of content and check the tone still matches your brand before your team relies on it.
  • Leave it alone if unsure. The defaults are chosen to work well; this screen is for teams with a specific reason to change them.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Brand Kit
docs.text: Your colours, fonts and logos, in one place — so everything GoodBards produces looks like it came from you.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
A brand kit is the visual half of your identity. Once set up, emails, social posts and generated images pick up your colours and logo without you specifying them each time.

It sits alongside the Voices Bank, which covers how your brand sounds. Together they are what makes AI output look and read like your brand rather than a generic template.

docs.title: How to set up your brand kit
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Settings → Brand & Context.
  2. Open the Brand Kit tab.
  3. Choose + Add Brand Kit.
  4. Add your colours, fonts and logo.
  5. Mark one kit as primary.

docs.title: Colour roles matter more than colour names
docs.text:
When you add a colour, you give it a role — what the colour is for, not what it is called. A colour named "Ocean Blue" means nothing to the platform; a colour assigned the role of primary or accent can be applied correctly everywhere.

If your generated designs use your colours in odd places, check the roles rather than the colours themselves.

docs.title: Applying your brand to the platform itself
docs.text:
Apply brand to app interface restyles GoodBards in your own colours and logo. Useful if your team should see their own branding rather than the GoodBards default.

This requires a primary brand kit. Until you mark one, the toggle explains that there is no primary kit yet.

docs.title: More than one kit
docs.text: You can hold several — useful for sub-brands or for an agency running different clients. The primary kit is the one used by default and the one that drives the interface.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Set this up early. Brand-aware content is only brand-aware from the moment the kit exists.
  • Use your real assets. Upload the actual logo files your designer produced, not screenshots of them.
  • Primary is the one that counts. With several kits, anything not explicitly told otherwise uses the primary.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: How the AI knows your brand
How the AI knows your brand
docs.text: Three things shape everything the AI writes for you: your Brand Context, the Brand Voice you pick, and what it has learned from working with you. This page explains what each one does and how to keep them right.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Without them, an agent writes generic copy and you re-explain your business in every request. With them, the same request comes back with your company's facts, in your style, following the rules you set.

What it is Who sets it When the AI uses it Brand Context Facts about your company: what you do, who you serve, how you are positioned, what never to say. Plus your primary Brand Kit (tone, keywords, hashtags). Your company admins, once. Every request, by every agent. Brand Voice A writing style learned from real samples, such as your founder's posts. Anyone builds voices; each person picks a default. Only when a voice is selected for the conversation. Memory Short facts learned from your conversations, or added by hand. Learned automatically, reviewed by you. In conversations with agents that have memory on.

Example. You ask: "Write a LinkedIn post announcing our webinar."

  • With nothing set up, you get a generic announcement.
  • With Brand Context, it names your product correctly, speaks to your target audience and never mentions pricing, because Guardrails says so.
  • With a Brand Voice selected, it sounds like your founder: short sentences, a question to open, no exclamation marks.
  • With Memory, it remembers you always add the registration link in the first comment, because you told it last week.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • To edit Brand Context, you need to be an administrator of your company account.

docs.title: How to set up your Brand Context
docs.text:
1. Go to Brand & Context → General Information.
  2. Choose Populate with AI and enter your Website URL: GoodBards reads your home page and a few key pages, and fills in the fields as drafts. This takes about a minute.
  3. Review each field. AI drafts are Hidden from AI until you choose Show to AI. A field you edit and Save becomes visible to AI.
  4. Fill in Guardrails → Never discuss with the topics the AI must avoid.
  5. On Marketing Campaigns, set your campaign defaults (audience, regions, objective).

See Brand & Context for every field.

docs.title: How to create a Brand Voice
docs.text:
1. Go to Brand & Context → Voices Bank and choose Create Voice.
  2. Give it a name, then add up to 10 samples of real writing: paste text with Add text sample, or choose documents with Add from Drive.
  3. The voice goes from Analyzing to Active in a few minutes. Open Details to read the profile it built: tone, structure, favourite phrases, do's and don'ts.
  4. To use it by default, go to Personal Settings → Preferences → Default brand voice. You can also pick a voice for one conversation from the Voice menu in the chat box.

docs.title: How to review what the AI has learned
docs.text:
• Company memory: AI Settings → Learned Memory. Facts shared by every agent and every user of your company. Each shows whether it was Learned from conversation or Added manually. Edit or delete any of them, or add one with Add To Memory.
  • Your own memory: Personal Settings → My Memory. Facts about you and how you work, seen only in your conversations. Turn Enable Personal Memory off to stop the AI using and collecting them.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Hidden fields never reach the AI. That includes every AI draft you have not reviewed yet. If the AI ignores something, check its badge first.
  • Changes take up to about ten minutes to reach the agents.
  • Only your primary Brand Kit is used. Its tone of voice, keywords and hashtags apply to every request; a Voices Bank voice applies only when selected.
  • A voice is applied when the conversation starts. Changing it halfway through has no effect; start a new conversation.
  • Company memory is shared with everyone in your company. Do not put personal or confidential details in it. Clear all memory cannot be undone.
  • Agents learn company facts only if allowed. An agent adds to company memory only when Promote Facts to Tenant is on in its settings (off by default). Learning starts after a conversation of several exchanges.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Brand & Context
docs.text: Everything GoodBards knows about your business — and what the AI is allowed to use when it writes for you.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
When an agent drafts an email or a social post, it needs to know who you are: what the company does, how it talks, who it competes with. This is where you tell it once, so you are not re-explaining your business in every prompt.

Get this right and everything the AI produces improves. Leave it empty and you get generic copy.

docs.title: The five tabs
docs.text: Tab What it holds General Information Company name, tagline, website and other basics. Brand Kit Colours, fonts and logos. See Brand Kit. Voices Bank How your brand sounds, so the AI writes in your voice. Marketing Campaigns Context about the campaigns you run. Competitors Who you compete with.

docs.title: How to fill in your company details
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Settings → Brand & Context.
  2. On General Information, fill in each field. Grey example text under each one shows the kind of answer expected.
  3. Changes save as you go.

docs.title: Controlling what the AI can see
docs.text:
Every field carries a badge showing whether the AI can use it:

  • Visible to AI — the agent may use this when writing.
  • Hide From AI — choose this to keep a field out of AI-generated content.

Most details are safe and useful to share. Hide anything commercially sensitive that you would not want appearing in a draft.

Populate With AI

Populate With AI, at the top right, fills these fields in by reading your website. It is a fast way to start — but read what it produces before accepting it, since everything the AI writes later builds on it.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Do this before generating content. Agents use whatever is here at the time they write. Filling it in afterwards does not improve drafts already produced.
  • Be specific. "We help companies grow" tells the AI nothing. What you sell, to whom, and what makes you different is what gets used.
  • Revisit it. When your positioning changes, update this — otherwise the AI keeps writing last year's message.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: Link GoodBards to the outside services your marketing depends on — social accounts, analytics, storage and more.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
GoodBards can only publish to a social channel, or report on your website traffic, if you have given it permission to reach that account. A connector is that link.

Most "why can't I see any data?" problems come back to a missing connector, so this is worth setting up early.

docs.title: How to connect a service
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Settings → Connections.
  2. Pick the category across the top — for example Social Media or Web Analytics.
  3. Find the service and choose Connect.
  4. Sign in to that service and grant the permissions it asks for. You are taken back to GoodBards when it is done.

Use Search connectors… to find one by name rather than hunting the tabs.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text: Category What it connects Social Media LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, Twitter (X), YouTube, TikTok. Instant Messenger Messaging platforms. Web Analytics Google Analytics, Search Console and similar. Digital Ads Advertising accounts. Storage External file storage. CRM Your customer relationship system. CMS Your website or content system. Email Email sending and mailbox services.

docs.title: Managing an existing connection
docs.text:
A connected service shows the account it is linked to, plus:

  • Manage Configuration — settings for that connector, such as which page or property to use by default.
  • Disconnect — removes the link. Anything relying on it stops working.

Connect the right account

The card shows which account is linked. On a shared channel, make sure it is the company account and not someone's personal profile — the person who connects it is the person whose access is used.

docs.title: Connectors your plan does not include
docs.text: Some connectors show a crown and a greyed-out Connect button. These are available on higher plans; speak to your account contact to enable them.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Connect before you build. Setting up a campaign for a channel you have not connected means going back and redoing the setup.
  • Connections can expire. If a service is failing, check here first — many providers require periodic re-authorisation.
  • Disconnecting is not retroactive. Already-published posts stay published; you simply cannot publish more until you reconnect.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Personal Settings
docs.text: Your own profile, password and preferences — the settings that affect you rather than your whole team.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Everything here is yours alone. Changing your language or your writing preferences does not affect colleagues, unlike AI Settings or Brand & Context.

docs.title: How to update your profile
docs.text:
1. Choose your profile picture at the top right, then Personal Settings.
  2. On Profile Information, update your details.

docs.title: Profile Information
docs.text: Field What it does Profile Image Your picture as colleagues see it. Full name Your name as it appears in the app. Role Your job title. Country Your country of residence. Custom Instruction Standing guidance for the AI when it writes for you.

docs.title: Custom Instruction is worth filling in
docs.text:
This is where you tell the AI how you like content written — for example a preference for bullet points over long paragraphs, or a particular tone. It applies whenever the AI generates something for you.

It is limited to 300 characters, so be specific rather than exhaustive.

Yours, not your company's

Custom Instruction is a personal preference. For how the AI should represent your brand, use the Voices Bank in Brand & Context.

docs.title: Password & Security
docs.text:
Change your password here, and turn on Two-Factor Authentication.

Turn on two-factor authentication

With 2FA enabled, signing in needs a verification code as well as your password. If your marketing account can email your entire contact database, it is worth protecting properly.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text: Interface preferences, including your language. You can also switch language from the EN control in the top bar.

docs.title: My Memory
docs.text: What the AI has remembered about you and how you work. Review it if the AI's output drifts from what you expect.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• These settings follow you, not the workspace. If you have access to more than one workspace, your personal settings apply across all of them.
  • Your name appears to colleagues. Fill it in properly if you work in a team.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Usage & Billing
docs.text: Track what your team has used against your plan, so nothing stops working unexpectedly.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
AI features consume credits. Generating copy, creating an image, running an agent — each uses some of your monthly allowance. This screen shows how much you have used and what has been driving it.

Worth checking monthly. Running out mid-campaign is avoidable if you can see it coming.

docs.title: How to check your usage
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Settings → Usage & Billing.
  2. Pick a period — 24h, 7d, 30d or 90d.

docs.title: What the numbers mean
docs.text:
Figure What it tells you Credits Used Your consumption in the selected period. Total Requests How many times an AI feature was called. Monthly Credit Quota The percentage of your monthly allowance used, with consumed and limit below. Daily Token Usage Day-by-day consumption, so you can see which days were heavy.

The Monthly Credit Quota dial is the one to watch. At 5% with three weeks to go you have plenty of room; at 80% with a week left, plan accordingly.

Tokens are a unit of AI text

Input tokens are what you send the AI, output tokens are what it returns. Longer prompts and longer responses both cost more. You do not need to manage tokens directly — the credit quota is the number that matters.

docs.title: The other tabs
docs.text: Tab What it shows AI Overview The summary described above. AI Request Details Individual requests, useful for tracing a spike. Guardrails Limits in place on AI usage. Models Which AI models were used.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Usage is shared across your team. The quota belongs to your company, not to each person, so a colleague's heavy week shows here too.
  • Check before a big campaign. Generating a large batch of content uses noticeably more than day-to-day work.
  • Investigate spikes. A sudden jump usually means a bulk generation job; AI Request Details will show what it was.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Sub-Workspaces
docs.text:
Run separate workspaces underneath your own — one per client, brand or business unit.

The app calls these sub tenants

You will see the word tenant on this screen. A tenant is simply a workspace — a self-contained account with its own data. This page uses "workspace", but the buttons say "tenant".

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
An agency running marketing for several clients does not want all that work in one pile. A sub-workspace is a self-contained space with its own contacts, campaigns and content, sitting under your main account.

Each has its own plan tier and its own credit allowance, so one client's heavy month does not consume another's.

If you run marketing for a single business, you will not need this.

docs.title: How to create a sub-workspace
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Settings → Tenant Settings.
  2. Open the Sub Tenants tab.
  3. Choose Create Sub Tenant.
  4. Give it a name and set its tier.

docs.title: Reading the list
docs.text:
Each row shows:

Column What it tells you Name The sub-workspace. Choose it to open. Tier Its plan — for example Pro. Users Who has access. Credit Usage Consumption against that workspace's own allowance.

The bar at the top right shows how many sub-workspaces you have against your limit — for example 1 / 5 tenants.

docs.title: Switching between workspaces
docs.text:
Use the workspace name at the top of the screen. Anything you then do — creating a campaign, adding contacts — happens inside the workspace you have selected.

Check which workspace you are in

The name at the top is the only thing distinguishing one from another. Before sending an email or publishing a post, confirm you are in the right workspace — content sent from the wrong one goes to the wrong audience.

docs.title: The other tabs
docs.text: Tab What it holds Preferences Workspace-wide preferences. Security Security settings for the workspace. Scheduled Tasks Recurring jobs that run automatically.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Data does not leak between workspaces. Contacts and campaigns in one are invisible to another. This is deliberate — it is what makes the separation safe for client work.
  • Each has its own credits. Check usage per workspace rather than assuming a shared pool.
  • Your limit depends on your plan. The counter at the top right shows how many more you may create.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Users, roles & permissions
docs.text: Invite your colleagues and decide, module by module, what each one can see and change.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Not everyone in your company needs everything. A sales colleague needs the contacts, not the ad budget; an agency client may only need the reports. GoodBards gives access per module, each in read-only or read-and-write, and bundles those permissions into roles you give to people.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • You need to be an administrator or the owner of your company account.

docs.title: The 12 modules
docs.text:
Access is given per module. They match the sections of the sidebar and of this documentation.

Module What it covers Home Home, the Daily Pulse, Actions, Calendar Audience Contacts, companies, segments, mailing lists Marketing Campaigns and tactics Emails and forms Emails, email designs, forms Events Event Management Social media Social posts and analysis Digital ads Digital Ads Content hub Content Workspace, Research & Plan, Content Repository, Translator Website and SEO Organic Visibility, Google Analytics, Google Trends AI studio Agentic AI Tool box QR codes, short links, chatbot, scheduler, image editor Settings Brand & Context, Brand Kit, connectors, AI settings

Each module is either read (see only) or write (see and change). A module someone has no access to disappears from their sidebar. Their own Personal Settings are always open to them.

docs.title: How to invite a user
docs.text:
1. Open Tenant Settings from your account menu, then the Security tab.
  2. Under Users, choose Invite User, enter their email and pick their role.
  3. They receive an invitation by email. The number of users your plan allows is shown above the list.

To change someone's role later, use the pencil next to their roles.

docs.title: The roles
docs.text:
Under Roles, the Platform roles are ready to use:

Role What they can do Tenant Owner Everything, plus billing and transferring ownership. Tenant Administrator Everything, plus users and company settings. Marketer Every module in read and write, and every contact. The usual role for your marketing team. Sales Home and the Audience only. With contact ownership on, they see only the contacts they own.

To give a group exactly the modules it needs, choose Create Role, name it, and pick the permissions. For example, a Reporting role with read access to Home, Marketing and Website and SEO, for a client who only follows results.

docs.title: Contact ownership
docs.text:
Each contact can have owners: the colleagues responsible for them. Turn on Restrict contacts to their owners to make people without the see every contact permission (the Sales role) see only the contacts and companies they own. Administrators and Marketers keep seeing everything.

Owners are assigned on the contacts list: select contacts, then Assign Owners. See Contacts.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Write includes read. Someone with write on a module can also see it.
  • Owners and administrators are never restricted. Their access cannot be reduced by a role.
  • Owners are recorded even when the restriction is off, so you can turn it on later without reassigning anyone.
  • API keys for connecting your own tools are on the same tab, below the roles. See Use the GoodBards API.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Social Media
docs.text:
Publish to your social channels and see how those posts performed.

Who sees it: everyone your administrator gives the Social media access to.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Social publishing needs the channel connected first. See Connections: without it, there is nowhere for a post to go.

docs.title: Social Post
docs.text:
Write a post for LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook or X, with the AI's help for the text and hashtags, then publish it now or schedule it. You can also turn an article into a series of posts.

See Social Post.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
How your social content performs across channels: reach, engagement and followers, post by post.

See Analysis.

docs.title: Social reports
docs.text:
Period reports per network (LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube), sent to you on a schedule if you want.

Guide coming soon

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text: See how your social content performed — reach, engagement, and how people reacted to it.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Posting is only half the job. This is where you find out whether anyone saw a post, whether they engaged with it, and whether the reaction was positive.

Use it to decide what to do more of. A post with high impressions but almost no clicks tells you something different from one with few impressions and strong engagement.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Your social account must be connected — see Connections.

LinkedIn organisation pages only

Report generation and analysis currently support LinkedIn organisation pages. Personal LinkedIn accounts are not supported, and the other channel tabs may have no report available yet.

docs.title: How to review social performance
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Social Media → Analysis.
  2. Pick a channel from the tabs across the top.
  3. Choose which organisation page to report on.
  4. Use the arrows beside the date to move between reporting days.

Choose Change beside the organisation name to switch to a different page.

docs.title: What the numbers mean
docs.text:
Metric What it counts What to read into it Impressions How many times your content was shown. Reach. Low impressions mean a distribution problem, not a content problem. Engagement Rate The share of people who interacted. The single most useful number here — it is reach-independent. Likes Straightforward approval. Easy to earn, weak signal. Comments People who wrote something. Far stronger than a like: it costs effort. Shares People who passed it on. The strongest signal of all. Clicks People who followed your link. The one that matters when the post has a destination.

Judge posts on engagement rate rather than raw likes. A post seen by 500 people with 50 interactions is doing better than one seen by 30,000 with 100.

docs.title: Content Sentiment Analysis
docs.text:
Beside the metrics, sentiment splits engagement into Positive, Neutral and Negative.

This is worth watching over time rather than per post. A shift towards negative sentiment is worth investigating early — it is easier to address a small complaint than a pattern.

docs.title: Top Posts Performance
docs.text: Below the summary, your best-performing content is listed with its engagement figures. This is the fastest route to understanding what your audience responds to: look for what the top posts have in common — format, topic, tone, time of day.

docs.title: History
docs.text: History, at the top right, holds previous reports so you can compare periods rather than judging a single day in isolation.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• One day is not a trend. Social performance is noisy. Compare across several reports before changing your approach.
  • Impressions depend on the platform. Reach is decided by each network's algorithm, so a drop is not necessarily about your content.
  • Match the metric to the goal. For awareness, watch impressions; for traffic, watch clicks; for community, watch comments and shares.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Social Post
docs.text: Write social posts with AI or from your articles, attach them to a campaign, then publish or schedule them to your connected accounts.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: A social post usually starts from something you already have, a blog article or a press release, or from a short idea. GoodBards drafts the post for each channel, checks it against the channel's limits and your brand, and publishes it from the campaign it belongs to, so its results show up in the campaign report.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A connected account. Connect LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X or TikTok under Connectors (in the menu behind your avatar), and choose the page to publish to in Destination. Without it, Publish and Schedule stay greyed out.
  • A campaign with a social tactic, to publish from.

docs.title: How to create posts from an article
docs.text:
Turn one article into a series of posts for several channels at once.

  1. In the sidebar, choose Content Hub → Content Repository.
  2. On the article, open the ⋮ menu and choose Create social posts.
  3. Under Campaign, choose the campaign the posts belong to, then Next.
  4. Tick the posts you want: Launch, Key figure, Question, In case you missed it. Each one shows when it is suggested to go out. Tick the channels.
  5. Check Link to the article. Add anything to emphasise under Anything to stress? (optional).
  6. Choose Write the brief, check it, then choose Generate.
  7. Click a post to review it, change its picture or plan it. You can close the window while the posts are written.

Nothing is published: every post waits on its channel as a draft for you to review.

docs.title: How to write a post with AI
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Social Media → Social Post, then New Post.
  2. Pick the Asset Type, for example a LinkedIn post.
  3. Under Creation Method, choose Write with AI, then Continue.
  4. Fill in What is it about?. Optionally add Source and materials (web pages or files from your Content Repository) and Tuning (audience, tone, language, keywords).
  5. Choose Write the brief, check it, then Generate. The AI drafts the post, reviews it and revises it once.
  6. Read the score and the checks. Apply the suggestions you agree with, or use Ask for a change. Then choose Save as asset.

In the post editor, Improve With AI rewrites within the channel's character limit and AI Hashtags suggests hashtags once the post has ten words. The preview on the right shows the post as it will appear on the network, on desktop or mobile.

docs.title: How to publish or schedule a post
docs.text:
Social Media → Social Post lists your posts as cards. The band on top shows whether a post is Scheduled or Published, and on which date.

  1. On Social Post, choose View Tactics on the post's card, then Add to Tactic. Choose the campaign and a compatible tactic, then Add to Tactic. (Or, from the campaign's social tactic, choose Import Asset and pick the post.)
  2. In the tactic, open the post's ⋮ menu:
    • Publish: choose the Destination and confirm.
    • Schedule: choose a Date & Time, or use AI Recommendations for the best slot, then Confirm Schedule.
  3. The card shows Scheduled or Published with the date.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Character limits are per channel: 3,000 on LinkedIn, 280 on X, 2,200 on Instagram and TikTok. The text box turns red past the limit.
  • Picture or link preview, not both. With a picture attached, LinkedIn and Facebook do not show the link's preview card. Without one, the preview card shows, but Instagram still needs a picture.
  • Published posts are locked. You cannot edit or delete them from GoodBards.
  • Posted outside GoodBards? In the tactic, choose Link published post and paste its link: its results then count in the campaign report.
  • LinkedIn personal profiles do not give analytics; publish to a company page if you want results.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.text:
Small standalone utilities for the everyday jobs around a marketing plan.

Who sees it: everyone your administrator gives the Tool box access to.

docs.title: Web Scraping
docs.text:
Pull the content of a web page so GoodBards can work with it, for example to brief the AI on a competitor's page.

See Web Scraping.

docs.title: External Chatbot
docs.text:
A chatbot on your own website that answers visitors' questions and captures leads as contacts.

See External Chatbot.

docs.title: QR Code Gen
docs.text:
Branded QR codes for print, packaging and events.

See QR Code Generator.

docs.title: URL Shortener
docs.text:
Short, trackable links.

See URL Shortener.

docs.title: Scheduler
docs.text:
Run an AI agent or a report on a schedule, every morning or every Monday, and receive the result by email or in your Content Repository.

See Scheduler.

docs.title: Image Editor
docs.text:
Crop, resize and adjust images without leaving GoodBards.

See Image Editor.

These tools work on their own. None needs a campaign before you can use it.

docs.title: External Chatbot
docs.text: Put a GoodBards agent on your own website, to answer visitors' questions around the clock.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Visitors ask the same questions at all hours — opening times, pricing, whether you serve their industry. The external chatbot puts one of your chat agents on your website to answer them, styled to match your brand.

Because it is one of your agents, it knows your business rather than reciting a scripted FAQ.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A chat agent to put on the site. See Chat Agents.
  • Someone who can add a snippet of code to your website.

docs.title: How to configure the chatbot
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Tool Box → External Chatbot.
  2. On the Settings tab, choose which Agent answers visitors.
  3. Write the Welcome message shown when the chat opens.
  4. Set the branding — icon, title, colours and sizes.
  5. Watch the Preview on the right update as you go.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
Setting What it controls Agent Which of your agents answers. Welcome message The greeting when someone opens the chat. Language The interface language of the widget. Theme Light or dark. Change Icon Your logo on the chat bubble. Square, up to 1 MB. Title Label The name at the top of the window. Font Size / Icon Size How large the widget appears. User / System Message Colours Colours for visitor and bot messages. Bubble Message The prompt on the closed bubble — for example Hi there! Need help?

The preview is live

The panel on the right shows exactly what visitors will see. Check it in both light and dark themes before publishing — colour choices that work in one can be unreadable in the other.

docs.title: Putting it on your website
docs.text: The Embed tab gives you the code to add to your site. Send it to whoever maintains your website, or paste it in yourself if you manage the site.

docs.title: Seeing how it performs
docs.text: Dashboard Analytics shows what visitors have been asking. Worth reviewing regularly — recurring questions usually mean something is unclear on your website, and the answer is often to fix the page rather than the bot.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Test it before launch. Ask the questions your customers actually ask and check the answers are right.
  • Your agent's knowledge is the bot's knowledge. If it cannot answer, improve the agent or your Brand & Context rather than the widget.
  • Say it is a bot. Visitors dislike discovering late that they were not talking to a person.
  • Keep a route to a human. Some questions need one — make sure the bot does not become a dead end.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Image Editor
docs.text: Crop, resize and adjust images without leaving the platform.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Marketing images rarely arrive the right size. A photo needs cropping for a banner, a logo needs resizing for an email header, a picture needs brightening before it goes out.

Small jobs like these do not warrant design software, and the editor handles them in place — so you are not exporting files back and forth.

docs.title: How to edit an image
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Tool Box → Image Editor.
  2. Load your image one of three ways:
  3. Drop it on the upload area, or choose it to browse.
  4. Paste URL to pull an image from the web.
  5. Load From Drive to use a file you already hold in Drive.
  6. Use the editing tools — crop, resize, filters and adjustments.
  7. Save the result.

docs.title: Supported formats
docs.text:
JPG, PNG, WebP and GIF.

Load from Drive to keep things tidy

If the image is already in Drive, use Load From Drive rather than downloading and re-uploading it. Fewer copies means less confusion later about which version is current.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Crop for the destination. An email header, an Instagram post and a website banner all want different shapes. Crop a copy for each rather than compromising with one.
  • Resize down, not up. Making a small image larger makes it blurry; the detail is not there to recover.
  • Keep the original. Save edits as a new file so you can go back if a later campaign needs a different crop.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: QR Code Generator
docs.text: Create QR codes for print, packaging and events — styled to match your brand.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: A QR code turns a printed thing into a link: a poster into a sign-up page, a business card into your website, a table tent into a feedback form. This tool makes them without a third-party site, and can track how often each one is scanned.

docs.title: How to generate a QR code
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Tool Box → QR Code Generator.
  2. Enter the destination in URL. The preview appears once the URL is valid.
  3. Style it to match your brand using the options below.
  4. Download the finished code.

docs.title: Styling options
docs.text:
Option Choices QR Style Squares, Dots, Fluid — how the code's dots are drawn. Color A set of preset colours, or the picker for your own. Marker Border Square, Rounded, Circle — the outer shape of the three corner markers. Marker Center Square, Circle — the inner shape of those markers. Center Logo Upload Logo places your logo in the middle.

Test before you print

Heavy styling can make a code harder to scan — pale colours, a large centre logo, or the Fluid style on a small print size. Always scan the finished code with a real phone before sending anything to print.

docs.title: Tracking scans
docs.text:
Track URL beside the URL field turns the code into a tracked link, so you can see how many people scanned it. This uses the URL Shortener behind the scenes.

Worth doing whenever the QR code goes somewhere you cannot otherwise measure — a printed flyer, a conference banner, product packaging.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• The code points at a URL, not a file. If the destination page moves, the printed code breaks. Use a tracked link so you can repoint it later.
  • Contrast matters. Dark code on a light background scans most reliably.
  • Size for the distance. A code on a poster read from across a room needs to be far larger than one on a business card.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Scheduler
docs.text: Run recurring work on a schedule: an AI agent's report every Monday, a social report every month, a web page checked every morning.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Some work is the same every week: summarise last week's results, check a competitor's page, collect the social figures for a client. The Scheduler does it for you at the time you choose, and sends you the result by email or saves it in your Content Repository.

docs.title: How to schedule a task
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Tool Box → Scheduler, then New Task.

  2. Give the task a Name and, if you like, a Description, then pick the Task type:

    Task type What it does Agent run Asks one of your AI agents a question, for example "Summarise last week's campaign results". Social report Builds the period report of one of your social accounts. Web scrape Reads a web page, for example a competitor's pricing page. Drive sync Brings files from a connected storage into your Content Repository.

  3. Choose Next, then fill in the Details: which agent and what to ask, which social account, which page. For an agent run, choose where the answer goes: an email to you or your colleagues, a document in your Content Repository, or both.

  4. Choose Next, then set the Schedule: how often and at what time.
  5. Save. The task appears in the list with its next run; open it to see the history of its runs.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• A task runs as the person who created it, with that person's access. An administrator can choose to run it as another member.
  • If the delivery fails, the run still counts. For example, the agent answers but the email cannot be sent: the history shows the run in amber with the reason.
  • A scheduled agent does not act on its own. When it runs unattended, it will not send a campaign email or publish content; it can prepare them for you.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Translator
docs.text: Translate marketing copy between the languages your markets speak, keeping the formatting intact.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Southeast Asia is not one audience. The same campaign may need English in Singapore, Bahasa in Indonesia and Chinese in Taiwan — and a translation that reads naturally in each.

The Translator works on formatted text, so headings, bold, lists and links survive. You can paste copy in or import a file.

docs.title: How to translate content
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Tool Box → Translator.
  2. Put your copy into Source Text — type it, paste it, or use Import File.
  3. Set Source Language and Source Region.
  4. Set Target Language and Destination Region.
  5. Choose TRANSLATE.

docs.title: Why region matters as well as language
docs.text:
The tool asks for a region alongside each language, and the pairing changes the result. Chinese for Singapore is not Chinese for Taiwan; English for Malaysia carries different conventions from English for the United States.

Setting both means you get copy that reads as though it were written locally, rather than a literal translation.

Formatting is preserved

Because the source box is a full editor, bold, headings, lists and links come through the translation. Format your copy before translating rather than reformatting afterwards.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Have a native speaker check anything important. AI translation is strong on fluency but can miss tone, idiom and cultural nuance — exactly the things that matter in marketing copy.
  • Translate the finished copy. Translating a draft you go on to edit means doing the work twice.
  • Watch length. Translated text often runs longer or shorter than the original, which can break a layout — check email and ad designs after translating.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: URL Shortener
docs.text: Turn long links into short ones, and see how often each is clicked.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Two reasons to shorten a link. It looks tidier in a social post, an SMS or on print. More usefully, a shortened link is a tracked link — you can see how many people clicked, which tells you whether a channel is working.

docs.title: How to shorten a link
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Tool Box → URL Shortener.
  2. Choose + New Link.
  3. Paste the destination URL and save.
  4. Copy the short link and use it wherever you need.

Before you create your first link, the list is empty — as above. Every link you create appears here with its click count.

docs.title: Finding a link later
docs.text: Use Search links… to find one by name or destination, and View to change which columns are shown.

docs.title: Where shortened links are used
docs.text:
Beyond links you create by hand, the shortener is used elsewhere in the platform:

  • The QR Code Generator uses it when you enable Track URL.
  • Links in emails can be tracked the same way, which is what click reporting is built on.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Shortened links are permanent-ish. Once printed or posted, you cannot take them back — so do not delete a link that is still in circulation.
  • Name links so you recognise them. Q4 flyer — Orchard Road beats a row of identical-looking codes.
  • One link per placement. Using a separate link for the flyer and the poster tells you which one worked. Reusing one link for both tells you nothing.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Organic Visibility
docs.text:
How your website is found, in search engines and in AI assistants, and what to fix first.

Who sees it: everyone your administrator gives the Website and SEO access to.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: These screens read your Google Search Console and Google Analytics data. If a screen says you are not connected, start at Connections.

docs.title: Performance & Report
docs.text:
How your site performs in search over time: clicks, impressions and position, with the trend and what to expect next. Other tabs give an executive report to share and a health check of your site.

docs.title: Page Fixes
docs.text:
The pages worth fixing first: pages close to the top of the results, pages losing traffic, and pages people see but rarely click. Each card says what to change, and you can send it to Actions.

docs.text:
Whether AI assistants can read, trust and quote your pages, scored page by page, and how often they mention you when asked about your market.

The searches and pages that are rising or falling right now, so you can act while it matters.
